slot.brief: Find the equation of the tangent (or normal) to a curve given implicitly or with an inverse trig form at a given point; moderate slope computation.

verdicts.working: At x=1/2, y=tan⁻¹(4/3). Differentiating gives y′ = [2(1+x²)/(1−x²)²]/[1+(2x/(1−x²))²], so y′(1/2)=8/5. The tangent is option A.

working:
$u=\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2},\quad 1+u^2=\dfrac{(1+x^2)^2}{(1-x^2)^2}$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{u'}{1+u^2}=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$; at $x=\dfrac12$, $m=\dfrac85$.
$y=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac43\right)$, so $y-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac43\right)=\dfrac85\left(x-\dfrac12\right)$

Independent check: At x=1/2, y=tan⁻¹(4/3). Differentiating gives y′ = [2(1+x²)/(1−x²)²]/[1+(2x/(1−x²))²], so y′(1/2)=8/5. The tangent is option A.
solution:
Using $u=\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2}$, we get $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{u'}{1+u^2}=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$, so at $x=\dfrac12$, the slope is $\dfrac85$. Also, $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac43\right)$ there; hence the tangent is
$$y-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac43\right)=\dfrac85\left(x-\dfrac12\right).$$

draft.distractor_notes: B uses the reciprocal slope; C gives the slope the wrong sign; D misses a factor of $2$ in the slope.
